newsitem.title: USA: Gunman killed after threating U.S. hydropower dam.
newsitem.headline: Gunman killed after threating U.S. hydropower dam.

text.p: A gunman was shot and killed outside the Bonneville Dam late Sunday after a tape-recorded threat was received against the hydropower facility, officials said Monday.

The shooting took place after workers at the dam visitors centre found a tape recorder with a note saying it should be played, said Diana Brimhall of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which operates the 57-year-old dam.
"On the tape was a threat to blow up Bonneville Dam and some other specific demands," she said.
The visitors centre was closed and staff members were evacuating when an armed man came onto the site. FBI, sheriff's deputies and state police had already arrived.
"There was a confrontation and the individual was shot and killed," Brimhall said.
FBI agents believe the gunman was responsible for the threat against the dam, although they did not immediately identify him or give details.

No explosive devices were found at the dam, about 40 miles (65 km) east of Portland, Oregon. The visitors centre, on the north side of the Columbia River in Washington state, remained closed while the FBI continued its investigation.
